regime: Labor Day Holiday (US Market Closed, No RTH Session)
summary: Quiet one. Monday September 7 is Labor Day, the US market is closed, and there was no regular session. The last completed session is Friday September 4, and the levels here are carried from that close. Friday's jobs day fade left the short term trend stops flipped down on NQ, ES and December gold, while crude held its rising stop as the lone long. VIX finished Friday calm near 14.5. Futures reopen Sunday evening on a holiday schedule, so expect thin liquidity into and just after the long weekend.
psychology: Days off are part of the job. A long weekend with no session is a good reminder that you do not need to be in the market every day to be a good trader. The edge is in waiting for your setup, not in forcing action. When the tape reopens after a holiday it is often thin, and thin tape can push price around on very little real buying or selling. Let the first hour or two of the reopen show its hand before you commit size. Patience through a quiet stretch is the same skill that keeps you out of a bad trade during a loud one.

event.surprise: Not applicable on a holiday. The next scheduled market driver is CPI mid month.

event.crossAsset: Carried from Friday: MES and December gold both closed lower with NQ and flipped their stops down; crude held at 91.24 as the lone long. VIX 14.53, still low. The market reopens for a normal session Tuesday Sep 8.

risk.sizing: Nothing changed over the holiday. Friday's jobs number whipped the tape and flipped the trend stops down on NQ, ES and gold, so the short term trend is no longer clearly up. Carry reduced size through the long weekend and into the Tuesday reopen. Do not chase the flip in either direction, and let thin post holiday tape settle before committing. Crude is the one clean long, above a rising stop, and can be sized normally with a stop under 89.42.
risk.openRisk: The flipped stops are the line for equities. MNQ back above 29,709 or MES above 7,746 on two hourly closes would turn the short term trend back up. Below, MNQ 29,468 and the 29,000 psych, and MES 7,710 then 7,700, are the downside references. December gold stays soft below the 4,496 stop; a reclaim there is the first repair sign. Crude stays long above 89.42.
risk.note: Labor Day is today, Monday Sep 7, and the US market is closed. Liquidity thins into the long weekend and can stay thin on the Tuesday Sep 8 reopen. Prop accounts should mind the holiday schedule and any lingering post news volatility. CPI lands mid month. Not financial advice.

fullReport.title: NY Opening Range / HTA OPEN
fullReport.html: No opening range today: the market is closed for Labor Day, so there is no 13:30 to 13:45 UTC window to compute. For reference, Friday's HTA OPEN read was an upside break out of the range at 13:50 UTC to a 29,692 high that failed and faded, closing back below NYVWAP, a classic upside fake out. On the Tuesday reopen the opening range resets fresh. All four plays (BIR, HOF, MID, BNC) are eligible on a Tuesday assuming no CPI or FOMC that day, but respect thin post holiday liquidity around the open.

fullReport.title: Momentum Breakout
fullReport.html: E3v2 Momentum Long keeps its filter off for the equity indices. NQ and ES both closed Friday below their trend stops, so a fresh momentum long would fight the tape. Crude sits above a rising stop, the profile a momentum long wants, but it recovered a dip rather than breaking out cleanly. No signal fires on a closed market; the filter carries this stance into Tuesday and keeps you out of index longs while the stops are flipped down.

fullReport.title: AVWAP Deviation Band
fullReport.html: Carried from Friday (MNQ): AVWAP center 29,537, close 29,524 right on the mean, about minus 0.5 sigma. Bands: plus 2 sigma 29,585, plus 1 sigma 29,561, minus 1 sigma 29,514, minus 2 sigma 29,490. Sigma tight near 24. Volume is unavailable on the continuous contract, so this is price only. There is no new band data today; the bands reset with the Tuesday session, and until then there is no clean 2 or 3 sigma extreme to fade.
